learn.title: Questions about characters
learn.body: The header `ctype.h` has functions that test one character, such as `isalpha` and `isdigit`, and functions that convert one, `toupper` and `tolower`. They work on a single `char`, not a whole string.

learn.title: Testing a char
learn.body: The `is...` functions give a nonzero number for true and 0 for false. Do not compare with 1, just use them in an `if`. Here `!= 0` turns the result into 1 or 0.

learn.title: Changing case
learn.body: `toupper` returns the capital version of a letter. Anything that is not a lowercase letter comes back unchanged.

learn.title: A char is a small number
learn.body: Each char is stored as a number, for example `'a'` is 97 and `'A'` is 65 in ASCII. So `'c' - 'a'` is 2, and `'a' + 3` is `'d'`. This is how you turn letters into positions 0 to 25.

learn.title: Shout a whole string
learn.body: Loop to the terminator and convert each char in place. It prints HELLO, C!. This is fine for plain English text.

learn.title: Letter to number

steps: `'e'` is the letter after `'d'`, but we use subtraction
That is 4, so `'e'` is the fifth letter
